error.description:
Error is a short, human-readable description of what went
wrong. The server never returns raw stack traces or DB
error strings here; the goal is to be informative without
leaking internals.

message.example: Please verify your email address first.
If the email exists, reset link has been sent
Registration successful! Please verify your email.
Email verification successful! You can now log in.

expires_at.description:
ExpiresAt is the RFC3339 timestamp after which the
captcha is no longer accepted. The client should request
a new captcha past this time.

id.description:
ID is the unique captcha handle; the client sends it back
to /api/captcha/verify to prove it solved the puzzle.

image.description: Image is the base64-encoded background PNG (data URL).

thumb.description: Thumb is the base64-encoded puzzle piece PNG (data URL).

thumbWidth.description: ThumbWidth / ThumbHeight are the puzzle piece dimensions.

thumbX.description:
ThumbX / ThumbY are the on-screen coordinates where the
client should place the puzzle piece. The puzzle is
always anchored at the right edge of the image; thumbX
is the horizontal offset.

token.description:
Token is the verification token, separate from the id. The
/verify endpoint requires both.

x.description:
X is the horizontal pixel offset where the user dropped
the puzzle piece.

y.description:
Y is the vertical pixel offset where the user dropped the
puzzle piece.

success.description:
Success is always true on a 200 OK; on failure the
endpoint returns a 4xx with an ErrorResponse body instead.

postCount.description: Non-database field: number of posts referencing the category by name

moderationReason.description:
ModerationReason records why the comment was rejected or held for
manual review (keyword hit, LLM verdict, or LLM failure).

llmReviewEnabled.description: Reject comments flagged by the LLM

related_post_id.description: Owning post ID for reply/comment notifications

type.description: Notification type: comment, like, reply, review, role

likesCount.description: Non-database field: used to include like count and whether the current user has liked in API response

postCount.description: Non-database field: number of posts referencing the tag

last_login_at.description: last login time to invalidate old tokens

message.example: Test email has been sent to your inbox

reason.example: I've been writing drafts and want to publish

action.description:
Action is "approve" or "reject". The service layer
rejects anything else.

reason.description:
Reason is a human-readable explanation shown to the
applicant in the notification. Optional.

put.description:
Sends a verification link to the new address when
SMTP is enabled, or applies the change directly
otherwise. The 200 response indicates the request
was accepted; the body distinguishes the two paths
via the `pending` boolean.

400.description: invalid payload / same email / email in use

get.description:
Consumes the single-use token from the verification
email. The same endpoint handles both new-account
verification and pending email changes; the
`require_relogin` and `new_email` response fields
appear only on the email-change path.
get.summary: Verify the email address (or a pending email change)

post.description:
The response is intentionally uniform: unknown
email, verified account, SMTP failure, and
database fault all return the same body. This
prevents callers from probing whether an address
exists and is unverified.

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's verification
flag and current email. Used by the frontend to
decide whether to show the "verify your email"
banner.

post.description:
Verifies the email and password, returns a signed
JWT for use in the Authorization header. The
captcha fields are required when the server is
configured to require captcha on login.

Consumes the single-use token from
/api/auth/password/reset/request and sets a new
password for the matching account.

400.description: invalid / expired token or invalid payload

post.summary: Reset password with an emailed token

post.description:
The response is intentionally uniform for every
outcome: an unknown address, an SMTP failure, and a
successful send all return the same body. This
prevents callers from probing whether an email is
registered.

put.description:
Updates the authenticated user's username, avatar,
birthday, and bio. Any field left out of the
request is left unchanged.

post.description:
Creates a new user account. The captcha fields are
required when the server is configured to require
captcha on registration. When email verification
is required, the response carries
`requires_verification: true` and the new account
cannot log in until it is verified.

put.description:
Updates the profile visibility and the per-field
hide flags. Any field left out of the request is
left unchanged.

get.description:
Returns a captcha id, token, and base64-encoded background /
puzzle images. The client solves the puzzle and submits the
coordinates to /captcha/verify. The captcha is single-use
and expires shortly after creation. This endpoint is rate-limited
per client IP.

post.description:
Consumes a captcha id and the puzzle coordinates. On success
marks the captcha as used so it cannot be re-submitted. The
verification result is held in the JWT and must be presented
alongside credential endpoints (login, register, etc.) that
require captcha verification.

400.description: invalid request, mismatch, expired, or already used

post.description: Contributors and above can create categories.

delete.description: Returns 400 if the category is still referenced by posts.

post.description:
Adds a comment to a post. Content is capped at 100
characters. The postId accepts either a number or a
string. The reply is held for moderation when the
manual review queue is on, the keyword filter rejects
it, or the LLM filter rejects it.

get.description:
Returns all published comments for the post. Pending
comments are only visible to the author and to admins
(the service layer filters by role).

delete.description: The author or an admin may delete a comment.

get.description:
Returns provider, endpoint and model with the API
key masked.

put.description:
Updates the AI provider, endpoint, and model. An
empty apiKey field leaves the existing key
unchanged.

get.description:
Asks the configured AI provider for the list of
models it currently exposes.

post.description:
Issues a small test prompt against the configured
provider to confirm credentials and endpoint are
wired up correctly.

get.description:
Returns captcha, registration, guest view, site
identity, and pagination defaults.

Returns the stored SMTP configuration with the
password masked.

put.description:
Updates the SMTP server, credentials, and sender
identity. An empty password field leaves the
existing password unchanged.

post.description:
Dispatches a small test message to the configured
test email (or to the current admin's address if
none is configured).

Accepts a multipart/form-data body with a single
'theme' part. The zip must contain a vexgo-theme.json
metadata file (either at the root or inside a single
subdirectory). Existing themes with the same id are
overwritten.

400.description: invalid zip / missing metadata / zip-slip entry

get.description:
Streams the preview.png from the theme directory.
Returns 404 if the theme, or its preview file,
does not exist.

Public — anonymous callers see the count but always
get `isLiked: false`. Authenticated callers see their
own like state.
get.summary: Read the like status for a post

post.description:
Idempotent toggle: likes the post on the first call
from a given user, unlikes on the second. The
response includes the new like count.

Issues a small test prompt against the configured LLM
to confirm the credentials and endpoint are wired up
correctly. The `response` field is whatever the model
replied with.

put.description: Moves the comment from pending to published.
Moves the comment from pending to rejected.

The optional rejectionReason is stored on the post and
shown to the author.

Authors can move a rejected post back into the
pending queue after editing. Only rejected posts
can be resubmitted.

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's notifications, paginated
and optionally filtered by type (comment, like, reply,
review, role) or read state.

Returns the number of unread notifications for the
authenticated user. Used by the frontend header to
render the badge.

404.description: notification not found or not updated

put.summary: Mark a single notification as read

get.description:
Returns the published post list, paginated and
optionally filtered by category or free-text search.
Anonymous callers see a reduced view (no
pending posts).

post.description:
Contributors and above can create posts. The `status`
field controls whether the post goes directly
to published, lands in pending for moderation, or
is saved as a draft.

get.description:
Used by internal callers (notifications, moderation) that
need to resolve a post id to its slug.
get.summary: Look up a post by numeric id

get.description:
All statuses (draft, pending, published, rejected) by
default; the `status` query param narrows to one.

Public for published posts; pending and rejected posts
are only visible to the author and to admins.

delete.description:
Authors can delete their own posts; admins can delete
any post. All comments on the post are removed in
the same transaction.

put.description:
Authors can update their own posts; admins can update
any post. Only the supplied fields are updated.

get.summary: Look up a post by slug

get.description:
Returns the slugs of every enabled SSO provider
(e.g. "github", "google") and whether the
local email/password login is allowed. The login
page uses this to decide which buttons to render.
Public endpoint — no authentication required.

Handles the redirect-back from the provider. On
success it returns an HTML page that writes the
result to localStorage and closes the popup; on
failure the same shape is used with an "error"
field. The frontend listens for the storage event
under the key `sso_callback_result` to pick up
the data.

parameters.description: state nonce from the original /login redirect
parameters.name: state

get.description:
Redirects the browser to the OAuth2 provider's
authorization endpoint. The `method` query
parameter controls the post-callback behaviour:
` sso_get_token` (default) issues a JWT for full
login; `get_sso_id` only returns the
provider-side user id (used to bind SSO to an
existing account).

302.description: redirect to the provider's authorization URL

get.description:
Returns the public post, user, comment, category and tag
counters. Anonymous callers see a reduced view that omits
pending posts; authenticated callers see the full set.

Most recently published posts, capped to the
requested limit.
Top posts by view count, capped to the requested limit.

post.description: Contributors and above can create tags.

delete.description: Returns 400 if the tag is still referenced by posts.

post.description:
Accepts a multipart/form-data body with a single 'file'
part. The stored filename is a freshly generated UUID
plus the sanitized extension from the original filename;
any untrusted characters are stripped before persistence.
Requires authentication.

Accepts a multipart/form-data body with one or more
'files' parts. Per-file failures are silently dropped;
the response only includes the rows that persisted.
Requires authentication.

delete.description:
Only the original uploader or an admin may delete a file.
The id is the MediaFile.ID from the upload response.

get.description:
Paginated list of users with optional free-text search
over username and email.

post.description:
Contributors and authors can apply to be promoted to
creator (a special author role with bulk publishing
permissions). The reason is shown to admins in the
review queue. One pending application per user at a time.

400.description: role not eligible or pending application exists

get.description:
Returns the creator application queue, paginated and
optionally filtered by status (pending, approved, rejected).

put.description:
Admins approve to grant the creator role; the optional
reason is forwarded to the applicant in the
notification.

400.description: invalid id, payload, or already processed

put.summary: Approve or reject a creator application

delete.description:
Admins can delete any non-super-admin user; super admins
can delete any user except themselves. All of the
deleted user's posts and comments are removed in the
same transaction.

403.description: admin delete restricted or no permission

put.description:
Admins promote/demote other users. Super admins can
also demote admins. Users cannot modify their own
role; super admins cannot be demoted.
